title: Native ports: games as plain Rust programs

units.title: Design the native port: a game as a plain Rust program
units.detail: june 2026-10-31 (d/modded-builds-are-plain-rust-programs-no-save): a modded build is literally a Rust program: no registers, no GBA memory block, no CPU, nothing preserved for save states or rewind; as regular and pretty as we can make it. Write docs/native-port-design.md covering: (1) where game state lives (globals as typed statics or one Game struct, from DWARF types where a decomp has them; a byte array only where types aren't known yet); (2) the hardware as a library, not memory (the runtime's PPU and sound behind an API like ppu.bg[0].scroll_x, the CPU gone; prior art: the SM64 and OoT PC ports' renderers); (3) the frame loop that replaces the main loop's V-blank wait, and interrupt handlers as callbacks; (4) function pointers as Rust fn values, and as IDs with a lookup table where the game does arithmetic on them (Emerald splits them into halves in task data); (5) ROM addresses as analysis-time facts only: return-address tricks like WarioWare's sub lr, lr, #24 resolved to a fixed destination at lift time (docs/research/code-without-rom-addresses.md); (6) holes: anything not statically resolved (undiscovered code, unresolved indirect jumps, RAM code, untyped pointer arithmetic) is a build error or a listed hole, since there's no interpreter fallback; (7) the oracle: the native program draws the same frames as the play build from the same inputs (the play build and its exact checks become the native port's oracle); (8) data pointers, DMA and struct copies, and what each needs. Read the existing analysis, structured codegen and mod-view designs first; cite the code. Propose the units that follow. Stop at ~3 h.

record.evidence: docs/native-port-design.md covers the card's 8 points with code citations and proposes 8 units (5 new filed). units.title: Spike: one of our agb programs as a native Rust program
units.detail: Take one of our own agb programs (agb/, our own source: small, no legal issues; one with a frame loop, input and a background or sprites, e.g. agb/template or agb/windows-blend) and lift it all the way to a native Rust program per docs/native-port-design.md: no Machine, no registers, no GBA memory map; state in Rust types, the hardware through the library API, a frame loop. Done when it draws the same frames as its play build (exact recompiled build) for the same input script over a few hundred frames, the code is committed, and the doc records what was hard, what was done by hand that the lifter should do, and what the next units should be. Stop at ~4 h with what's measured. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): no agb/ program reads input, so first write a new agb/native-spike (agb source only; D-pad moves a sprite and scrolls a background; SCENE.md). The native program lives in its own crate (crates/native-spike or agb/native-spike-native, your call) and takes the desktop's flags: --headless --frames N --input <script> --frame-hashes F. Done when: native and the exact play build give identical --frame-hashes files over 600 frames of a script that moves something at least every 60 frames, and one planted wrong store makes them differ.

Findings: docs/research/native-agb-spike.md. Branch t3/a5d53ea7, unmerged.

units.title: Hole report: what blocks a native build of each game
units.detail: A tool (Rust, not bash) that lists, for a ROM, everything that blocks a pure native build per docs/native-port-design.md's hole list: code reached in runs or fuzzing that discovery didn't find; indirect jumps and calls not resolved; return-address arithmetic (the scrambled-return-address side-by-side tool from docs/research/code-without-rom-addresses.md finds it, e.g. WarioWare's IWRAM helper); code run from RAM; pointer arithmetic or casts the known types don't explain, where types exist. Run it on the eight games of that research (Emerald, Kirby, Metroid Zero Mission, Minish Cap, WarioWare, moonbeam and the rest) and write each game's counts and worst holes into docs/research/native-holes.md, ranked by how close each game is to native. Propose discovery or fuzzing units aimed at the commonest holes. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): put the hard-hole classification in the analysis crate (the lifter reuses it). Runs: the research doc's 5,400-frame press script through the interpreter's coverage, for all eight ROMs listed by file name. Untyped pointer arithmetic: report 'not measured until stage B'. Rank by hard holes, then bytes reached but not discovered. Done when native-holes.md's counts match the tool's output on all eight, and the controls hold: WarioWare's 0x3000468 lr-24 helper listed as a hole, moonbeam's __gnu_thumb1_case_* resolved, Emerald's unresolved-jump count equals Recovery's.

record.evidence: just holes on all eight ROMs (5,400 frames, research press script): each first line identical to docs/research/native-holes.md's ranking lines (Metroid 18, WarioWare 22, moonbeam 23, Kirby AM 29, Kirby NiDL 30, Emerald 34, Minish Cap 46, Rogue 86). Controls: WarioWare 0x03000468 site-24 listed NOT resolved; moonbeam __gnu_thumb1_case_uqi/uhi (0x08042e00/14) resolved; Emerald 11 unresolved = Recovery's 670-659 (just discover). Classification in analysis::holes, cargo test -p analysis holes 10 passed. Review: fresh subagent, 11 findings fixed or documented (b251fd00). just check, disc-pret, disc-agb, jt-score pass.

units.title: Emerald: ten functions as native Rust, scored against pret
units.detail: Like {unit:mod/decomp-spike}, but native per docs/native-port-design.md: ten Emerald functions of varied shape (a leaf getter, an array loop, a call chain, a switch, struct field access, u8/u16 arithmetic, one that stores a function pointer; ClearBattleMonForms and SeedRngAndSetTrainerId among them) lifted to plain Rust over typed state from pret's DWARF, with no registers, Machine or addresses. Emerald is the measuring stick, not the goal: score each against pret's C (statements, named accesses, loop shapes, anything left raw), and say what the lifter needs for each gap. Check behaviour where it can be: the same results as the play build's function on the same inputs (fn-diff style). Write side-by-sides and scores into docs/native-port-design.md. Never copy pret's C text into the repo ({d:mod-view-prints-pret-s-file-line-never-pret-s-c}). Stop at ~3 h. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): mirror-safe (decision): lifted code and side-by-sides go in mods/emerald/native-ten/ (left out of the public mirror); docs/native-port-design.md gets only scores and gaps. The ten: {unit:mod/decomp-spike}'s eight (mods/emerald/decomp-spike/) plus CalcCRC16 and GetBgAttribute; reuse its scoring columns. Behaviour check: a native form of fn-diff (entry state as guest-layout RAM + params from {unit:native/summaries}; compare RAM, I/O, return value, ignoring stack below sp). Done when it prints 'native 0 of 10 differ' and a one-byte edit gets caught.

record.evidence: just native-ten: 'native 0 of 10 differ' (3,072 runs), ROM-byte fault under Random caught 671/672; verifier's own one-byte edits (CalcCRC16 0x8408->0x8409, GetBgType arm) caught; 19 hand edits caught. Review by fresh subagent: 6 findings fixed (8372fdfe). just check passes.

No bar (decision: measure only): the tool prints agree/disagree/no-proto counts and per-category disagreement counts, 10 per category checked by hand, numbers quoted in the design doc. A unit test where a function clobbers r4 fails its proof.

units.title: Lift report metrics and a bars file the lift check holds
units.detail: docs/native-stage-b.md, 'How every piece is checked' and piece 0. Shared code every stage-B unit needs. (1) gbaa-lift writes its metrics into report.txt as `name value` lines, split by region so later bars mean something: lines of src/main.rs; functions lifted, recognised, replaced, unrecognised; functions with a summary hole; four-register functions without a summary hole; byte loads/stores at a constant address per region (RAM, I/O, ROM, VRAM/palette/OAM); at a computed address per region where the value set says, else unknown; sp-relative loads/stores; call_fn calls; jumps by value; stand-ins; gap targets (codegen::native's count() today lumps these). (2) `--bars FILE` fails the lift when any metric is over its bar (maxima only; a unit that needs a relation adds a metric whose bar is 0), naming it. (3) The program list moves out of the lift-check recipe into the same committed TOML (one table per program: ROM, route, flags, bars) read by a Rust driver (a gbaa-lift or route-check mode), so later units add a program by adding a table, not bash ({d:stage-b-checks-are-bars-in-one-committed-file}). Bars start at today's values; only lowered. Done when: just lift-check runs from the TOML and passes; a codegen test lowers one bar below the measured value and the lift fails naming that metric; the planted store and planted hard hole are still caught; just check passes.

units.title: Fallthrough into another function keeps r4-r11 and flags
units.detail: docs/native-stage-b.md, piece 1. Stage A prints a fall (or jump) into another function's entry as a tail call, so the continuation starts with r4-r11 and NZCV zeroed (codegen::native goto/call_then). Real agbcc games do this. units.title: Function flow passes only registers a callee reads
units.detail: docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'Registers nobody reads'. The function flow (crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs) passes r0-r3 to every callee and takes all four back, read or not, so a function's address left in a scratch register travels the whole program: on native-irq-hold, as built on the branch unit/native/fnref-unknown-addrs, the handler's pool word 0x080001bc goes in r3 through 39 calls and 36 returns of 26 functions that never touch r3, to the reset's swi, where all four registers count as given to the BIOS. That un-proves the two handler words main proves and costs the program its 16 typed heap accesses. (With every kind of memory read switched off, GBAA_FNREF_OFF, 13 of affine's 39 words left are given to the BIOS, most by this road, but in a flow the switches changed: it shows the road, not a count.) Work on that branch (it has the object split, RAM pointers, GBAA_FNREF_WATCH; not on main). Give a callee only the registers its summary reads and take back only those it sets (codegen::saves; all four where the summary has a hole); a swi holes only the registers its BIOS call reads; a call whose target is still empty in an early round must not pass its registers to every function without a direct caller for good. Done when: unit tests for each; native-irq-hold's words 0x080001bc and 0x080001c0 are no longer first held by a register passed or returned unread (GBAA_FNREF_WATCH), and the evidence says what holds them next, or that they are proven; fn_words_not_proven and the other counts no higher than the branch's on any program. The branch doesn't land here: {unit:native/fnref-ram-pointers-land} does.

notes.text: Since PR 8 (metroid-entry-reads) a callee may also take r4-r11 (Summary::takes/may_take): narrowing what a call gives must keep those. The flow doesn't give them yet: {unit:native/fnref-taker-regs}.

units.title: Function flow: the object split and RAM pointers land
units.detail: The branch unit/native/fnref-unknown-addrs holds three units' work on crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs that isn't on main: frames and allocation sites as objects ({unit:native/fnref-heap-sites}), call-site context, off by default ({unit:native/fnref-context}), and RAM pointers followed ({unit:native/fnref-unknown-addrs}), with the metric fn_loads_read_everything (623 load sites on affine at the start, 3 now; barred in every table of lift-check.toml on the branch) and GBAA_FNREF_WATCH. june's answer (q/unknown-address-step-land-without, 2026-11-12): land it on that count, once native-irq-hold has its 16 typed heap accesses (ref_accesses) back, every other bar held, or raised with its cause named. On 2026-11-13 twelve bars are over (docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'Why the branch doesn't land'): native-irq-hold loses its two handlers' proven words (0x080001bc, 0x080001c0) and with them ref_accesses 16 to 0; ref_unexplained rises about 42 on native-bios-more, -bios-region, -dma and the spike because every call_fn set, all the address-taken functions, grows by the words now read; native-tasks has complete sets where main has none. Also unexplained: native-bios-calls' 571 loads that read everything. Done when: main merged into the branch, native-irq-hold's ref_accesses is 16, each bar over is back or raised by hand with its cause in the evidence (just tracker decide --for-run), the branch is merged, just lift-check and just check pass.

units.title: Function flow: pointers into stack frames kept exact
units.detail: docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'Kinds of read switched off'. On affine, with GBAA_FNREF_OFF (unsound, measuring only; on the branch unit/native/fnref-unknown-addrs, as is all of this) the loads that read everything alone leave fn_words_not_proven at 55, reads through a pointer anywhere in an object alone leave it 55, and both off give 41: the two must be made exact together, and both are about stack frames. (1) The 3 loads left that read everything (affine 0x08000a24 to 0x08000a2c) go through a pointer into a caller's frame at or above the callee's entry sp, which Run::load_at gives up on (G::obj_up): follow it to the callers' frame objects through the sp each call passed. (2) A pointer into a frame moved by an index the run doesn't know becomes anywhere in the frame and reads every word of it: keep it in its stack slot (crates/codegen/src/native/frame.rs has the slots), and keep an array of pairs' fields apart (an offset known modulo the stride; core::fmt's argument arrays hold a value and a function each, affine 0x080036e4). Work on that branch (it has the object split, GBAA_FNREF_WATCH and GBAA_FNREF_OFF). Done when: unit tests for each; fn_loads_read_everything is 0 on affine and no higher anywhere; fn_words_not_proven falls on affine (the switches say up to 14 words; say in the evidence how close it got and what holds the rest) and rises nowhere. The branch doesn't land here: {unit:native/fnref-ram-pointers-land} does.

units.title: Function-flow branch merged with main's Ref tokens
units.detail: The branch unit/native/fnref-unknown-addrs (head 233ba6c0) holds three units' unlanded work on crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs: frames and allocation sites as objects, call-site context (off by default), RAM pointers followed, the metric fn_loads_read_everything, and the tools GBAA_FNREF_WATCH and GBAA_FNREF_OFF. Main's {unit:native/fnref-emerald-speed} (f52fe115) rewrote about 1,000 lines of the same file: large pile, every-cell and ROM reads are one lazy token each (Tok::Ref, Src, Xf, G::expand). Merging main into the branch gives 22 conflicts in fnref.rs (G::store, give, give_all, Val::cap, Run::block, load_raw, call_by_value, follow, and more: that PR's 'For whoever merges' lists them), one in fnref/tests.rs and one in lift-check.toml; beyond the conflicts, the branch's own reads (every object's cells, a run of RAM, an object's cells, the lost-pointer cell) and its tokens (Tok::Obj, Tok::RamFrom) must work with Ref tokens, and the watch trace must see through them. docs/research/fnref-held-words.md was measured before that commit and says so. Done when: the branch builds merged with main, its and main's fnref unit tests pass, Emerald's flow still finishes (main's time and memory within a tenth), and every table of the research note is measured again on the merged code and the note corrected (drop its 'before main's Ref tokens' paragraph): just lift-metrics on every program, GBAA_FNREF_OFF's rows on affine (set as one comma list; check the lift prints the switches it saw), the first-road table from GBAA_FNREF_WATCH=all, native-irq-hold's handler words. Then record {unit:native/fnref-unknown-addrs} with the re-measured finding if it stands. The branch doesn't land here: {unit:native/fnref-ram-pointers-land} does.

units.title: The IRQ wrapper's second half is discovered and lifted
units.detail: Found by the review of {unit:native/lift-psr-boot-irq}, 2026-11-13. The agbcc-shape IRQ wrapper (Metroid 0x08000104 and its IWRAM copy 0x03000c7c, Nightmare 0x03001030, Emerald 0x08000248, Rogue 0x0800025c, Imperium 0x08000264) calls its handler with 'add lr, pc, #0; bx r0' (Metroid 0x08000204). analysis::vsa::func::classify makes a bx a call only right after 'mov lr, pc', so this one is a jump, discovery has no code at its return site (0x0800020c), and the wrapper's second half (ldm, mrs cpsr, msr cpsr back to IRQ mode, IE and IME stores, msr spsr, bx lr) is in no lift. The lifter prints the call and then unreachable!("a call that never returns returned") (seen in Metroid's lift with the dispatcher stand-in dropped), so a lifted wrapper panics when its first handler returns. That is why the corpus counts 3 msr/mrs per wrapper where the code has 6, and why the games' IRQ-dispatcher stand-ins can't go yet (the reset stand-ins can). Do: have discovery take 'add lr, pc, #0' (lr = the address after the bx) as the call it is, so the return site is the same function's code and PsrFns prints its msr/mrs (if it comes out as its own function instead, PsrFns::place must cover it). It changes discovery for every program and the play build: run the scored checks (disc-*, jt-score) and the full just lift-check. Also add a standing check that runs printed PSR statements: today no lift-check program does (agb's wrapper keeps its stand-in in all 14; that unit's PR says how a hand run with --drop-standin 0x03000000 went). Smaller things from the same review: an sp write after a wrapper's mode switch is no longer a stack-switch hole in these functions (crates/codegen/src/native/frame.rs, the comment near line 451 is stale there); a wait or an ordinary function's I/O store while still in IRQ mode writes Game::sp with the IRQ-mode sp. Done when: Metroid and Nightmare lifted with their dispatcher stand-ins dropped print all six PSR statements of each wrapper and no unreachable! after the handler call; a native check that runs a lifted wrapper's whole path is in lift-check; lift-check, the scored checks and just check pass.

units.title: Function flow gives a callee the r4-r11 it takes
units.detail: Since {unit:native/metroid-entry-reads} a direct call passes a callee the r4-r11 it reads at entry (Summary::takes; x_<key> with the caller's own), and so do the indirect calls a holes file's [[takes]] names. The function-address flow (crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs, Edge::Call) still gives a callee r0-r3 only, so a function pointer or a table's address that reaches a taker in r4-r11 is missing from its entry state, and a callee set built from it can be called complete when it isn't. Metroid's one chain passes a constant that is only stored, so its lift is unaffected; a hand-written callee that calls through a taken register would be. Fix: give all registers at a direct call to a function with may_take() != 0 and at the named indirect calls, as Edge::Tail does. Done when: a test program (or unit test) whose taker calls through a pointer it was passed in r8 gets that callee in its set; just lift-check passes.

units.title: An agb program whose function takes r8 from its caller
units.detail: From {unit:native/metroid-entry-reads}: no lifted program that runs under the native check has a function that takes r4-r11 from its callers (every agb program's report says 0 functions take), and Metroid's 600 frames from boot don't reach its save writer. So the printed passing call, the named indirect call's match and a taker's stopping plain entry are checked by unit tests of the summaries and by the crate building, not by a run against the interpreter. Add an agb test program with a hand-written assembly function that reads r8 and r9 as its caller left them (one called by bl, one through a pointer named in holes/<name>.toml's [[takes]]), draws what it read, and add it to crates/codegen/lift-check.toml with a planted control. Done when: just lift-check passes with it, and its report says 2 functions take.
